Theorem  
For every bigrassmannian \(v=v_{r,s,t,n}\in S_n\), with
\[
1\le t\le r,s\le n,\qquad t>r+s-n,
\]
put
\[
i=s-t+1,\quad j=r-t+1,\quad
a=\min(n-r-i,r-j),\quad b=\min(i,j),
\]
\[
A=\Lambda/I_{r,n-r},\qquad Q=J_v/A_+J_v.
\]
Then both
\[
G_L=\{\bar s_{(i^j,\rho)}:\rho\subseteq b^a\}
\]
and
\[
G_R=\{\bar s_\mu:i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq((i+a)^b,i^{j-b})\}
\]
map to homogeneous integral bases of \(Q\). Hence both families minimally generate \(J_v\). Moreover
\[
Q\cong\bigoplus_{\rho\subseteq b^a}\mathbb Z[-(ij+|\rho|)],
\qquad
H_Q(z)=z^{ij}\binom{a+b}{a}_z,
\]
so \(Q\) is torsion-free. Partition conjugation induces a graded integral isomorphism
\[
J_v/A_+J_v\cong J_{v^\vee}/A_+J_{v^\vee}.
\]

Hypotheses  
All notation is as in the theorem; \(I_{r,n-r}\) is the Grassmannian Schur ideal, \(A_+\) is the positive-degree ideal of \(A\), and \(\rho\subseteq b^a\) includes the singleton empty partition when \(a=0\).

Consolidated proof  
Let
\[
F_L=\bigoplus_{\rho\subseteq b^a}\mathbb Z e_\rho,\qquad
e_\rho\longmapsto[\bar s_{(i^j,\rho)}]\in Q.
\]
Task 296 proves this homogeneous map is surjective and has zero kernel: a nonzero homogeneous kernel element would yield a forbidden source-form homogeneous syzygy, after rewriting its decomposable side using the generating family. Thus \(F_L\cong Q\), proving that \(G_L\) is an integral homogeneous basis.

If a member of \(G_L\) were removable as a generator of \(J_v\), its residue would be generated by the remaining residues in \(Q=J_v/A_+J_v\), contradicting that these residues form a basis. Hence \(G_L\) is minimal.

Task 301 supplies the graded integral involution induced by \(\omega(s_\lambda)=s_{\lambda'}\), taking the relevant Grassmannian quotient and basic ideal to their conjugates. Task 286 verifies the conjugated parameter admissibility and identifies the conjugate of the lower-adjoined basis with \(G_R\). Therefore \(G_R\) is likewise a homogeneous integral basis of \(Q\), and is minimal.

The degrees of the lower basis elements are \(ij+|\rho|\). Summing over \(\rho\subseteq b^a\) gives
\[
H_Q(z)=z^{ij}\sum_{\rho\subseteq b^a}z^{|\rho|}
=z^{ij}\binom{a+b}{a}_z.
\]
Task 264 verifies that conjugation descends to \(Q\), preserving grading, integral torsion, and degreewise ranks. Since \(Q\) has the displayed integral basis, it is torsion-free.
